extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems with full step-by-step solutions. It is designed to measure mathematical problem-solving ability across subjects and difficulty levels.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATH problems are created by the Mathematical Association of America (MAA). AMPS consists of problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MATH problems from the Mathematical Association of America (MAA); AMPS problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy code, including Khan Academy modules.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each MATH problem has a full step-by-step solution written in LaTeX and natural language; the paper says problems come with "full step-by-step solutions" and that "all MATH problems also include answer explanations".
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No annotation quality analysis or inter-annotator agreement is described for the MATH dataset in this section.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward high school competition mathematics from specific U.S.-centric contests and subjects, and difficulty is organized by AoPS-style levels. It may therefore overrepresent competition-style problem solving rather than broader mathematical reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MATH is challenging and accuracy remains low even for large models; scaling model size alone is unlikely to solve it. The paper also notes that generated step-by-step solutions can be misleading or logically wrong, and that using models' own generated solutions at test time can reduce accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper suggests potential positive impact through improved mathematical reasoning and interpretability, but also notes a possible negative implication: strong performance could have ramifications for cheating on homework.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No explicit personal sensitive information is collected in MATH itself. The paper does mention human participants' attitudes toward mathematics and educational status in evaluation, but not as dataset attributes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking/testing mathematical problem-solving ability, and the step-by-step solutions can also be used for training/fine-tuning models to generate derivations and explanations. AMPS is described as a pretraining corpus.
